properties.name: Ādaži Military Base
properties.note: The article on the town of Ādaži calls it the largest military base of the Latvian National Armed Forces and places it in the village of Kadaga, across the river. The marker is at Kadaga.

properties.name: Ādaži military training area
properties.note: Mapped as a military training area ("Ādažu poligons").

properties.name: Lielvārde Air Base
properties.note: Military air base (ICAO: EVGA). The article says it forms the core of operations of the Latvian Air Force.

properties.name: Latvian Naval Forces, Liepāja
properties.note: The naval branch of the National Armed Forces has its headquarters in Liepāja. The source names only the city, so the marker, set on its Karosta district, is approximate.

properties.name: Selonia Military Training Area
properties.note: Mapped as a military training area ("Sēlijas militārais poligons"). OpenStreetMap marks its own outline as approximate.

properties.name: Mežaine military training area
properties.note: Training area of the 4th Brigade of the National Guard near Skrunda, on the site of the former Soviet radar town Skrunda-1.

properties.name: Audriņi air surveillance radar
properties.note: The article on the village says an air search radar of the Latvian Air Force was built on its outskirts in 2004. The marker is the village, not the radar.

properties.name: Šiauliai Air Base
properties.note: A major facility of the Lithuanian Air Force and one of the bases of NATO's Baltic Air Policing mission.

properties.name: Rukla
properties.note: Units of the Lithuanian Armed Forces are based in the town, which has hosted NATO's Enhanced Forward Presence since 2017. The marker is the town.

properties.name: Gaižiūnai training area
properties.note: Mapped as military land ("Gaižiūnų poligonas").

properties.name: Pabradė Training Area
properties.note: A major military facility about 4 km north of Pabradė. The marker is the town.

properties.name: Rūdninkai Training Area
properties.note: Military training area south-west of Vilnius, re-established in 2022. The article says it is to host the German 45th Panzer Brigade.

properties.name: Brig. Gen. Kazys Veverskis training area, Kazlų Rūda
properties.note: Mapped as military land ("Brg. Gen. Kazio Veverskio poligonas", formerly Kazlų Rūdos poligonas).

properties.name: Lithuanian Naval Force, Klaipėda
properties.note: Mapped as military land under the name of the Naval Force of the Lithuanian Armed Forces ("Lietuvos kariuomenės karinės jūrų pajėgos").

properties.name: Karmėlava
properties.note: The article on the town says radar information about the airspace over the Baltic states is collected here and passed on to NATO. The marker is the town.

properties.name: Ämari Air Base
properties.note: Military air base (ICAO: EEEI). It has hosted NATO Baltic Air Policing patrols since April 2014.

properties.name: Tapa Army Base
properties.note: Army base of the 1st Infantry Brigade. The article lists a NATO Enhanced Forward Presence battalion among the units housed there.

properties.name: Central Training Area (Keskpolügoon)
properties.note: Mapped as a military training area ("Kaitseväe keskpolügoon").

properties.name: Nursipalu training area
properties.note: Mapped as a military training area ("Nursipalu harjutusväli").

properties.name: Taara Army Base, Võru
properties.note: Army base in Võru, run by the 2nd Infantry Brigade.

properties.name: Naval Base, Tallinn (Miinisadam)
properties.note: Mapped as a naval base ("Mereväebaas", also known as Miinisadam).

properties.name: Kellavere radar station
properties.note: Marked on the article's map of Estonian Air Force locations as a radar station.

properties.name: Suwałki Gap
properties.note: The sparsely populated area around the Polish–Lithuanian border, between Belarus and Russia's Kaliningrad exclave, which the article describes as of great strategic and military importance. An area, not a site: the marker only names it.

properties.name: Bemowo Piskie
properties.note: The village is the site of the training base of NATO's Enhanced Forward Presence battlegroup in Poland. The marker is the village.

properties.name: Naval Support Facility Redzikowo
properties.note: A United States missile defence site (Aegis Ashore) at the airfield just north of the village, operational since 2023. The marker is the village.

properties.name: 22nd Air Base, Malbork
properties.note: Polish Air Force base east of Malbork.

properties.name: Baltiysk
properties.note: The article calls the town a major base of the Russian Navy's Baltic Fleet. The marker is the town.

properties.name: Kaliningrad (Baltic Fleet headquarters)
properties.note: The article gives Kaliningrad as the headquarters of the Baltic Fleet. The marker is the city.

properties.name: Chkalovsk air base, Kaliningrad
properties.note: Naval air base 9 km north-west of Kaliningrad.

properties.name: Chernyakhovsk air base
properties.note: Military air base of the Baltic Fleet, 4 km south-west of Chernyakhovsk.

properties.name: Donskoye air base
properties.note: Air base in Kaliningrad Oblast, close to Russia's westernmost point; the article says its pads are used by helicopters.

properties.name: Pionersky Radar Station
properties.note: Russian early-warning radar station.

properties.name: Pskov airport
properties.note: An airfield used both as a military air base and as a civil airport; the article says a military transport aviation regiment is based here.

properties.name: Ostrov air base
properties.note: Air base 7 km south-east of Ostrov, listed as an army aviation airfield.

properties.name: Vladimirsky Lager
properties.note: A locality in Pskov Oblast with a military base; the article says a motor rifle brigade has been stationed there since 1993. The marker is the locality.

properties.name: Kamenka
properties.note: The article says a motor rifle brigade is located at this settlement on the Karelian Isthmus, with a tank training range to its east. The marker is the settlement.

properties.name: Levashovo air base
properties.note: Air base on the northern edge of Saint Petersburg, mostly transport aircraft and helicopters.

properties.name: Pushkin Airport
properties.note: Air base 28 km south of Saint Petersburg; the article says a helicopter regiment is based here.

properties.name: Kronstadt
properties.note: The article names Kronstadt as a base of the Baltic Fleet. The marker is the town.

properties.name: Vysotsk
properties.note: The article on the town says it hosts a base of the Baltic Fleet. The marker is the town.

properties.name: Lekhtusi Radar Station
properties.note: Russian early-warning radar station.

properties.name: Lida air base
properties.operator: Belarusian Air Force and Air Defence Forces
properties.note: Air base at Lida, Grodno Region.

properties.name: Baranovichi air base
properties.operator: Belarusian Air Force and Air Defence Forces
properties.note: Air base south of the city of Baranavichy (ICAO: UMMA).

properties.name: Machulishchy air base
properties.operator: Belarusian Air Force and Air Defence Forces
properties.note: Air base at Machulishchy, Minsk Region.

properties.name: Luninets air base
properties.operator: Belarusian Air Force and Air Defence Forces
properties.note: Reserve air base at Luninets, Brest Region.

properties.name: Baranavichy Radar Station
properties.note: Russian early-warning radar station in Belarus.

properties.name: Vileyka VLF transmitter
properties.note: Russian radio transmitter in Belarus, listed as part of the Russian Navy.

properties.name: Gotland Regiment (P 18), Visby
properties.note: Armoured regiment based in Visby, re-established in 2018.

properties.name: Karlskrona Naval Base
properties.note: The largest naval base of the Swedish Navy.

properties.name: Muskö Naval Base
properties.note: Underground naval facility on the island of Muskö, south of Stockholm.

properties.name: Upinniemi naval base
properties.note: The village is dominated by a Finnish naval base, home to the Coastal Brigade among other units. The marker is the village.
